intro: Sending a request here does one thing: we put what you wrote in front of the independent HVAC companies that cover the area you picked. Nobody from this site arrives at your house. You deal directly with the company that takes your job, from the first phone call to the final invoice.

sections.h: What happens when you hit send
sections.p: Your request goes into our system with the name, phone number, email address if you gave one, the service area you selected, the kind of work you picked and the description you wrote. We match it to the companies that cover that area and pass it on. You do not need an account and there is nothing to sign. If the submission does not go through, the form tells you rather than pretending it worked.

They read the description and call you. They ask their own questions, because nobody can see your system from a form. Expect to be asked what the outdoor unit is doing, whether the air is warm, whether the breaker holds, and how old the equipment is. Then they decide what the job needs, set their own appointment, and tell you what the work involves and what it costs before they start. Everything after that first call is between you and them.

sections.h: Why we ask for your area
sections.p: So the request reaches companies that work your part of the metro and can actually get to the house. A company that does not cover your street would have to turn the job down, and you would lose time for nothing. We also ask what kind of work you need so the request lands with a company that takes that kind of job. We would rather send it to the four companies that cover Spring than to a list of thirty that do not.

sections.h: What determines the price of AC repair
sections.p: What a job costs depends on the equipment, its age, which part has failed, whether the trouble is in the refrigerant, the coil, the wiring or the airflow, and how hard the unit is to reach. Only the technician who can open the panel can price it, which is why there is no price on this site. Any number printed here would be a guess dressed up as a quote.

sections.h: How we choose the company that takes your job
sections.p: We send your request to the HVAC companies covering your area. They are on the list because they work that area and hold a current license, not because they bid for your job. We do not run an auction, and we do not pass a request to anyone who has not agreed to work that area. We also do not stop you from going elsewhere. You can say no to whoever calls, ask for a second opinion, or hire somebody else entirely. If you hire somebody else, there is nothing to settle with us, because you never made a contract with us.

sections.h: Check the license before anyone starts
sections.p: Ask the company for its Air Conditioning Contractors license number, then look it up yourself in the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation license search at tdlr.texas.gov. Check that the status is active and that the name on the license matches the company you are dealing with. A company with a real license will not mind you doing this. Ask the same question about liability insurance, and get the estimate in writing before anyone opens a panel.

sections.h: Emergency AC repair when the system fails on a hot afternoon
sections.p: Say in the description that the house is heating up and you have no cooling, and pick Emergency AC Repair in the service list. Say whether the outdoor unit is silent, humming or running, and leave a phone number somebody can answer. Emergency requests go to the companies covering your area that take emergency work. We do not promise an arrival time, and nobody from this site is coming to your door, so if you need somebody there now, say so on the phone, or call the number at the top of the page. While you wait, set the thermostat to fan only, open the doors between rooms to move air, and check the AC breaker once if the outdoor unit has stopped.

sections.h: What we do and what the contractor does
sections.p: We take your description, make sure it reaches the companies working your street, and answer anything you send us. The contractor does the rest: they send the technician, diagnose the system, quote the work and carry it out. We do not have an office, a shop or a walk-in door, and we do not stand behind the warranty a contractor gives you. What they take responsibility for, they take responsibility for.
